sections.h2: How would you describe Putnam County to a home seller?
sections.html:
Putnam County had 21,218 residents in 2010, 22,047 at the 2020 census and an estimated 23,722 in July 2025. Eatonton levies its own city tax, and the tax commissioner runs the county's billing from putnamgatax.com.

Older people shape the market. Residents 65 and over make up 27.1% of the population, children under 18 make up 17.9%, and households average just 2.17 people. Per person income is $48,458, the highest of the four counties compared, and 31.1% of adults have finished a four-year degree.

The county spans 344.68 square miles of land with 64.0 people per square mile. Shoppers spent $321,128,000 at Putnam retailers in 2022, or $14,003 per resident, and medical and social service providers took in $55,842,000. Employers numbered 546 in 2023, with 5,509 jobs and a payroll of $264,921,000, up 5.6% in jobs from a year earlier.

sections.h2: What do Putnam County home values show?
sections.html:
An owner-occupied home in Putnam has a middle value of $249,300, between Polk and Pike on the Census table. Owners live in 80.9% of housing units.

Monthly housing costs run $1,522 for owners with a loan and $485 for owners without one. The county has 14,017 housing units but 10,435 households, a gap of roughly 3,600. Not every Putnam property is someone's legal residence, so ask the assessors whether yours carries a homestead exemption before you promise a buyer a particular tax figure.

sections.h2: What do Putnam County's household and work numbers add?
sections.html:
The county has 10,435 households and 1,590 veterans. The Census table puts Black residents at 24.7%, higher than in any other county of the four, and Hispanic or Latino residents at 8.6%. People born abroad are 7.6% of the total, and 11.2% of residents over 5 use another language at home.

Just 53.9% of people over 16 hold or seek a job, a lower share than Pike or Polk, and seniors account for 27.1% of the population. Mean travel to work is 31.1 minutes. Accommodation and food services sales were $31,508,000 in 2022, and 2,492 businesses have no employees. Broadband subscriptions cover 86.6% of households, and the same 86.6% of adults hold a high school diploma.

Disability affects 13.8% of residents under 65, and 16.6% in that age group lack health insurance. For an owner on a fixed income, an unpaid tax bill and a deferred repair list are the two problems most likely to push a sale.

sections.h2: Which Putnam County office does what?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner collects, and the Board of Tax Assessors values.

  • Tax Commissioner: collects property, timber and heavy duty equipment tax. Payments can be made on the website, by phone with a card, by mail, or at the office.
  • Tax Assessors: (706) 485-6376, with parcel records at qpublic.net/ga/putnam.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: intangible tax and deed copies, in the courthouse.
  • Marine equipment specialist: an assessor staffer who handles boats.

The commissioner publishes a Taxpayer Brochure that walks through returns, exemptions and appeals, and the Department of Revenue's county sheet points to putnamgatax.com for the commissioner and putnamcountyga.us for the county.

sections.h2: What are the Putnam County payment dates and penalties?
sections.html:
December 1 is the date for real and personal property. The commissioner mails those bills by October 1. Mobile homes follow a separate calendar: bills by February 1, payment by April 1, and a decal is no longer required after a resolution dated July 2, 2021.

Interest starts accruing one day late, then posts again each month on the 1st. The rate is the prime rate in force at the start of the year plus 3%. At 120 days a 5% penalty arrives, with another 5% for each further 120-day period, to a ceiling of 20%. A mobile home pays a flat 10% beginning the day after its due date.

Homesteaded property owing less than $500 skips the 90-day penalty described on the office's page. The commissioner mails each bill to the owner, never to the lender.

sections.h2: If I sell mid-year, who gets the Putnam County bill?
sections.html:
The seller of record on January 1 gets the first bill. Once a new deed is recorded, the commissioner sends the buyer a copy as well.

The office's advice is to read your closing papers or ask the closing attorney who owes the money. For a seller, that means checking that the contract and the settlement statement spell out the year's tax, regardless of whether closing lands before or after December 1.

Boats follow the same January 1 logic. Sell one and the fall bill still comes unless the assessors' marine specialist is told. Only accounts totaling $20,000 or more in marine equipment get a bill.

sections.h2: How can Putnam County owners appeal or reduce a bill?
sections.html:
Your first appeal goes to the assessors, who may revise the value and mail a second notice. If they hold at the same number, the file is forwarded for a hearing. An arbitrator is another option, and the county's FAQ sets 45 days from the notice date for it.

  • Homestead: own and occupy on January 1, file at the assessors, and get the paper in before April 1.
  • Age 70: owners who reach it can request an extra homestead exemption.
  • Relief grant: the 2023 state grant cut assessed value by $18,000 on homesteaded property, and the commissioner says it returns for tax year 2026. Rentals and non-homesteaded property were not eligible.
  • Refund: a claim for tax wrongly collected has to begin within three years of the payment date.

The final step in a dispute is Superior Court, started by written notice to the assessors.

sections.h2: How are Putnam County bills calculated and spent?
sections.html:
The formula starts at 40% of fair market value, subtracts exemptions, then applies the millage rate. The county commissioners, the school board, the City of Eatonton and the State of Georgia each adopt a rate, with one mill worth $1 per $1,000 of taxable value.

The county lists what the money buys: schools and county government, public buildings, bridges and roads, courts, the jail and law enforcement, fire protection, and public health and sanitation. The assessors take real estate returns during the first three months of the year.

sections.h2: What happens in Putnam County if tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
A FiFa can be recorded 30 days after the commissioner sends a 30-day notice. Because it is a public lien record, the FAQ warns it can reach credit bureaus once a bill is more than 90 days late.

The tax sale is generally annual, held at the courthouse on the first Tuesday of July. Registration opens at 9 am, and bidders must show photo ID, pay in certified funds and settle the same day by 4 pm. No electronic bidding exists, and owners with delinquent county accounts cannot register. The list is published in The Eatonton Messenger and on Georgia Public Notice.

Paying the commissioner's payoff at closing keeps your property off that list.

faqs.q: What date are Putnam County taxes due?
faqs.a: December 1 for real estate and business personal property. Mobile home taxes are due April 1.

faqs.q: Does Putnam County auction delinquent properties?
faqs.a: Yes. It generally holds one sale a year, on the first Tuesday in July at the courthouse, with in-person bidding only.

faqs.q: Who owes tax if my Putnam County house sells in mid-year?
faqs.a: The January 1 owner is billed first, and the buyer later receives a copy. Your closing attorney and contract decide who pays.

faqs.q: How is the Putnam County late penalty set?
faqs.a: Interest runs at the January prime rate plus 3%. A 5% penalty follows at day 120 and repeats every 120 days until 20%.

faqs.q: Where do I find a Putnam County parcel record?
faqs.a: At qpublic.net/ga/putnam, or by calling the assessors at (706) 485-6376.
